findings.failure_mode: Server-Side Request Forgery via /preview URL parameter
findings.trigger: An unauthenticated attacker sends GET /preview?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (cloud metadata), or http://127.0.0.1:PORT/admin (internal services), or an internal-only host such as http://internal-db:5432/. The Flask server performs the request from its own network position and returns the first 2000 characters of the response body to the attacker.
findings.evidence:
public.py:9-11 `url = request.args["url"]
    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
    return resp.text[:2000]`
findings.business_impact: The attacker gains read access to internal-only network resources and cloud instance metadata (which frequently contains IAM credentials), enabling credential theft, lateral movement, and full compromise of cloud infrastructure. Any user who can reach the public /preview endpoint is harmed; the organisation's internal services are exposed.
attack_chain: public.py:9-11 - The attacker-supplied 'url' query parameter is read directly from the request with no validation, allowlist, scheme restriction, or host/IP filtering, then passed straight into requests.get().

Fails here: There is no check at all: no scheme allowlist (file://, gopher:// etc. may be attempted depending on the requests/urllib3 version), no blocklist of private/loopback/link-local IP ranges (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.x/172.16.x/192.168.x), no DNS-rebinding protection, and no authentication or authorization on the route. The server fully trusts the client-supplied URL.
